2609.35376.title: How Well Can LLMs Simulate Real Learner Evaluations of Educational Feedback?
2609.35376.paper_summary: While recent studies have explored human behavior and preference simulation using large language models (LLMs), it remains unclear how well LLMs can simulate subjective evaluations from real learners in educational settings. We investigate this question using real learner evaluation data on feedback for high-school biology questions at both the group and individual levels. We compare performance with and without learner-specific information, such as personality traits and evaluation examples, across six models. Our results show that LLMs still have a limited ability to simulate learner evaluations. Providing learner profiles and examples improves score calibration and individual-level simulation, but more often fails to improve group-level consistency. These findings highlight the need to investigate which learner information and adaptation strategies are effective for learner preference simulation.
2609.35376.paper_summary_zh: 雖然最近的研究已經探討了使用大型語言模型（LLMs）進行人類行為和偏好模擬，但目前尚不清楚LLMs在教育環境中能多好地模擬真實學習者的主觀評價。我們使用真實學習者對高中生物問題的反饋評價數據來調查這個問題，涵蓋了群體和個體層面。我們比較了在有和沒有學習者特定信息（如個性特徵和評價示例）的情況下，六個模型的表現。我們的結果顯示，LLMs在模擬學習者評價方面仍然能力有限。提供學習者檔案和示例改善了分數校準和個體層面的模擬，但更常見的是未能改善群體層面的一致性。這些發現突顯了調查哪些學習者信息和適應策略對學習者偏好模擬有效的必要性。
